speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, such as when they started and if they're worsening? Also, have you had any recent injuries or exposures that might be relevant?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the skin lesions have a central clearing or target-like appearance, and have you noticed a tick bite on your body recently? Have you experienced any severe headaches, neck stiffness, or facial drooping?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the vesiculopustular lesions and recent camping in Minnesota, this presentation is highly suggestive of Southern Tick-Associated Rash Illness (STARI) or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, but the specific lesion morphology is key. Have you noticed any rash on your palms or soles, and have you been prescribed or taken any antibiotics for these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands are a classic sign of secondary syphilis, which can also cause arthritis and fever, rather than a tick-borne illness given the lesion morphology. REQUEST TEST: RPR and Treponemal Antibody Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative syphilis tests, let's pivot back to the tick-borne possibilities suggested by the Minnesota camping trip. REQUEST TEST: Lyme Disease Antibody Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, monoarticular wrist arthritis, and painful violaceous pustules on the extremities is highly characteristic of Erythema Chronicum Migrans (EM) and Lyme arthritis, but the negative serology is puzzling. Let's rule out other tick-borne illnesses common in Minnesota, such as Anaplasmosis or Babesiosis, which can present with fever and joint pain. REQUEST TEST: Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR and Babesia microti PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative tests for Lyme, syphilis, and other common tick-borne illnesses, I suspect a different viral or bacterial cause. Could you describe the exact appearance of the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, and have you had any recent contact with sick individuals or pets?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: The migratory nature of your joint pain, combined with fever and violaceous lesions on the hands and feet, is highly characteristic of Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease caused by Coxsackievirus A6. I will now confirm this clinical diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (Coxsackievirus A6)
